documentation: Where each corvidae workspace lands in the public target that receives it. Corvidae's own directory is not the target's: `components/chat` is cinder's `packages/chat`, and `components/cinder` is cinder's `packages/components`. Without this table the transform would emit a second `components/**` tree beside the target's real `packages/**` one and duplicate every package, which the deletion rule cannot clean up because a path the transform does not emit is never pruned. `package-surface.json`'s `provenance.path` is deliberately not reused for this: it records where a package's published surface was vendored from, points `@lostgradient/operative` at a repository that no longer exists, and is `null` for the four packages that have never been published. Which target a workspace ships to is decided by `targetFor` in `manifests.ts`, so it is not repeated here; this table answers only where inside that target the workspace lands. `emit` carries the target-relative directory. `deferred` is a workspace whose placement is genuinely unresolved: the transform emits nothing for it and the sync refuses to run, naming the issue that must rule on it.

@lostgradient/weft.reason: The weft target is a single-package repository whose one workspace is `packages/weft`. Unchanged.

@lostgradient/cinder.reason: Cinder publishes `@lostgradient/cinder` from `packages/components`, not from a directory named after the package. `target-owned.json` already carries a `fields` entry keyed to `packages/components/package.json` preserving cinder's `"prepare": "cd ../.. && husky"`; that entry can only match once this remap is in place.

@lostgradient/weft-ui.reason: Routed to the cinder target, because `targetFor` gives the weft target exactly one member. It was `packages/weft-ui` in the weft monorepo it merged from and keeps that directory name here.

@lostgradient/operative.reason: Library directory, unchanged downstream. Its `package-surface.json` provenance points at the retired agent-bureau repository, which is why that field is not the source of truth for layout.

@lostgradient/testing.reason: Cinder already carries `packages/testing` as its private `@cinder/testing` workspace, which is the same workspace under its old name.

@lostgradient/typescript.reason: The cinder target holds the shared TypeScript configuration as an ordinary workspace, so every emitted tsconfig can extend it by specifier. The weft target vendors a copy instead, which `typescript-configuration.ts` places relative to the package rather than through this table.

@lostgradient/desktop.reason: Excluded from the mirror by the repository owner, 2026-09-21 (`package-map.json` carries the `exclude` ruling), so no placement is needed and the plan never consults this entry. The application was the SvelteKit `chat-room` when that ruling was made and is now an Electrobun desktop application; the rename removes the specific name collision with cinder's `labs/chat-room` (`@cinder/chat-room-lab`) but not the reason for the ruling, which is that a public library mirror has not been ruled on as a home for a private desktop application whose toolchain is a Hutch-managed devkit projected outside version control. It stays `deferred` rather than being given a directory so that if the exclusion is ever lifted, the placement has to be ruled on before anything is emitted.

@lostgradient/playground.reason: Excluded from the mirror (`package-map.json` carries the `exclude` ruling), so no placement is needed and the plan never consults this entry. COR-1201 moved cinder.website onto this application and deleted the public cinder repository's former copy at `packages/playground` in cinder#1602. It stays `deferred` rather than being given a directory, as `@lostgradient/desktop` does, so that lifting the exclusion forces a ruling on placement before anything is emitted.

@lostgradient/evaluation.reason: Excluded from the mirror in `package-map.json`, so no placement is needed. New in this repository and never published, and no workspace the mirror emits depends on it. `deferred` rather than a directory, matching every other excluded workspace here, so the sync refuses rather than guessing if the exclusion is lifted.

@lostgradient/terminal.reason: Excluded from the mirror in `package-map.json` by the owner ruling of 2026-09-25 (not published until a later publication project), so no placement is needed and the plan never consults this entry. COR-482 created the workspace. It stays `deferred` rather than being given a directory, matching `@lostgradient/desktop`, so that lifting the exclusion forces a ruling on placement before anything is emitted.

@lostgradient/ventriloquist.reason: Excluded from the mirror in `package-map.json` by the owner ruling of 2026-09-25 (not published until a later publication project), so no placement is needed and the plan never consults this entry. COR-482 created the workspace; its only consumer is `@lostgradient/terminal`, which is itself excluded. It stays `deferred` rather than being given a directory, matching `@lostgradient/desktop`, so that lifting the exclusion forces a ruling on placement before anything is emitted.

@lostgradient/telephone.reason: Excluded from the mirror in `package-map.json`, so no placement is needed. New in this repository and never published: it carries an Operative agent run onto the chat stream wire, and its only consumer is `@lostgradient/desktop`, which is itself excluded — so nothing the mirror emits depends on it. `deferred` rather than a directory, matching every other excluded workspace here, so the sync refuses rather than guessing if the exclusion is lifted.

openQuestions: The cinder target's root manifest declares `applications/*`, `components/*`, `packages/*` and `internal/*` as its workspace globs. After this remap, `applications/*` and `components/*` match nothing corvidae emits; they are kept because a glob that matches nothing is harmless while narrowing the list could drop a workspace the target owns. Cinder's own root manifest lists `labs/chat-room`, which none of the emitted globs covers, so the emitted root already removes that lab from the target's workspace graph. `@lostgradient/desktop` itself is excluded from the mirror by owner ruling (2026-09-21), so nothing corvidae emits reaches that path either way.

`@lostgradient/weft-ui` lands in the cinder target at `packages/weft-ui` purely because `targetFor` gives the weft target one member. The weft repository carried its own drifted copy at the same path; COR-1192 rules that copy retired rather than synced, which `target-owned.json`'s `retired` section records and the transform carries out. Three things now move together if the weft repository is ever meant to receive weft-ui again: that routing, this entry, and the retirement.
